turns.line: We now stand ten years past the midpoint of a century that has witnessed four major wars among great nations. Three of these involved our own country. Despite the carnage of these conflicts, America is today the strongest, the most influential and most productive nation in the world. We are understandably proud of this preeminence, yet we realize that America's leadership and prestige depend, not merely upon our unmatched material progress, riches and military strength, but on how we use our power in the interests of world peace and human betterment.

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: Throughout America's adventure in free government, such basic purposes have been to keep the peace; to foster progress in human achievement, and to enhance liberty, dignity and integrity among peoples and among nations.

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: We pray that peoples of all faiths, all races, all nations, may have their great human needs satisfied; that those now denied opportunity shall come to enjoy it to the full; that all who yearn for freedom may experience its spiritual blessings; that those who have freedom will understand, also, its heavy responsibilities; that all who are insensitive to the needs of others will learn charity; that the scourges of poverty, disease and ignorance will be made to disappear from the earth, and that, in the goodness of time, all peoples will come to live together in a peace guaranteed by the binding force of mutual respect and love.

turns.speaker: B
turns.line: Well, it depends on what you mean.

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: For example, we could bring back the death penalty for murder, give longer prison sentences for lesser offences and lock up juvenile offenders.

turns.speaker: B
turns.line: Those really sound like Draconian measures. Firstly, what do you do about miscarriages of justice if you've already put innocent people to death?

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: You'd only use capital punishment if you were absolutely sure that you'd convicted the right person.

turns.speaker: B
turns.line: But, there've been many cases of wrongful conviction where people have been imprisoned for many years. The authorities were sure at the time, but later it was shown that the evidence was unreliable. In some cases, it'd been fabricated by the police.

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: Well, no system of justice can be perfect, but surely there's a good case for longer prison sentences to deter serious crime.

turns.speaker: B
turns.line: I doubt whether they could act as an effective deterrent while the detection rate is so low. The best way to prevent crime is to convince people who commit it that they're going to be caught. It doesn't make sense to divert all your resources into the prison system.

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: But if you detect more crimes, you'll still need prisons. In my reckoning, if we could lock up more juvenile criminals, they'd learn that they couldn't get away with it. Soft sentences will merely encourage them to do it again.

turns.speaker: B
turns.line: Yes, but remember that prisons are often schools for criminals. To remove crime from society, you really have to tackle its causes.

turns.line: Thank you, Bob! This past week has been the beginning of Armageddon for many, a series of unprecedented meteorological events occurred around the world. turns.speaker: Mike
turns.line: Moving to to Latin American, Ecuador has suffered a six month drought that has not only affected farming, but has also forced the closure of the hydroelectric power plant that provides electricity for the entire country. In Chile, a major earthquake that registered seven point five on the Richter scale struck the southern region. Losses are reported to be in the billions. Authorities have not yet released an official statement.

turns.speaker: Bob
turns.line: Not a great week for the world! Any good news?

turns.speaker: Mike
turns.line: I'm afraid not, Bob. One of the major volcanoes in Mexico has erupted, causing major floods and landslides in the region. turns.line: Can't it wait? I'm watching the game right now!

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: Your friends and family are coming over tonight and we still need to get a lot of things.

turns.speaker: B
turns.line: Fine! What do you need?

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: Ok, pick up some cured meats to go with the wine. Maybe a pound of polish sausages, ham, liverwurst, salami and any other cold cuts that are on sale. I think I saw a promotion for pastrami. Also get some cole slaw and a jar of olives.

turns.speaker: B
turns.line: Whoa wait a minute! Isn't that a bit too much? I mean, how much is all of this going to cost!

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: Never mind that. Get some dips as well. Get a jar of spinach and blue cheese dip and also some Tzatziki. If they have bean dip get that as well. Last but not least, get some pickles.

turns.speaker: B
turns.line: Is that all, your majesty?

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: Very funny! Get a move on! People will be here any minute.

turns.speaker: John
turns.line: Ok darling, got some pizzas, potato chips, hot dogs and lots of cheese!

turns.speaker: Kelly
turns.line: Oh John, I thought we said we would start eating right! Remember? Our new healthy lifestyle? That's all junk food!

turns.speaker: John
turns.line: Hrumph! Right, so what did you get?

turns.speaker: Kelly
turns.line: Well, healthy food , of course! I got some whole wheat bread, skimmed milk, fresh fish and organic carrots. . . .

turns.speaker: John
turns.line: Organic? What's organic? Do we need organic carrots. . . ?

turns.speaker: Kelly
turns.line: They were grown without using any chemicals that are harmful to our health. And yes, John, we need organic carrots. . . .

turns.speaker: John
turns.line: Oh, so organic vegetables are the ‘green' option, right?

turns.speaker: Kelly
turns.line: Yup, better for the environment and better for us!

turns.speaker: John
turns.line: Wait a minute, that? . . . Doughnuts? they organic doughnuts, Kelly?

turns.speaker: Kelly
turns.line: . . . . I like doughnuts.

turns.speaker: Mark
turns.line: Thanks a lot for pitching in once again Judy, we really appreciate your help. It seems that at this time of year there are more and more people who are struggling to make ends meet. There aren't many professional chefs like you who are so generous with their time.

turns.speaker: Judy
turns.line: Don't be silly Mark, I'm more than happy to donate my time to a good cause. Volunteering at the soup kitchen has been really rewarding for me. You know, it's satisfying to provide good meals for those who are less fortunate, I feel like I'm really making a difference in some small way.

turns.speaker: Mark
turns.line: Well, your skills are definitely appreciated here! The people who come here have fallen on hard times and a delicious hot meal can really bolster their spirits. That smells great! The needy are sure lucky to have you!

turns.speaker: Judy
turns.line: Thanks Mark!

turns.speaker: Judy
turns.line: Here you go, enjoy your meal! Old lady: Thank you my dear, Oh this looks lovely.

turns.speaker: Judy
turns.line: You're welcome, Hello sir, today we have. . . . are you doing here?

turns.speaker: George
turns.line: Hey Judy! I'll have a little of everything, thanks. . . . smells great!

turns.speaker: Judy
turns.line: George, seriously . . . what are you doing here? I haven't seen you since our divorce was finalized. You've got no right to be here, you're hardly homeless!

turns.speaker: George
turns.line: Don't be like that Judy, I really miss your home cooking!

turns.speaker: Je
turns.line: Joanne, let's not make this divorce any more acrimonious than it already is, okay? Let's just get down to business and start dividing this stuff up fairly, so we can go our separate ways, alright?

turns.speaker: Joanne
turns.line: Fine with me. I just want to get this over with. It's important we make a clean break. I should have signed a pre-nup.

turns.speaker: Je
turns.line: What was that?

turns.speaker: Joanne
turns.line: Nothing! Anyway, you're right, there's no reason this has to be nasty. My lawyer tells me you've accepted our alimony proposal and the division of property, as well as the custody agreement- I keep the cat and you get the dog. So that's done. . . . finally.

turns.speaker: Je
turns.line: Let's not go there, Joanne! Ok, so let's start with the record collection, I'll take the albums I contributed and you can have your cheesy disco albums back.

turns.speaker: Joanne
turns.line: Fine, but I'm keeping the antique gramophone as my grandfather gave it to me.

turns.speaker: Je
turns.line: I believe that was a wedding present to both of us, Joanne. And you hardly ever use it!

turns.speaker: Joanne
turns.line: He's my grandfather, and he never really liked you anyway!

turns.speaker: Je
turns.line: Whatever! Alright, I'll concede the silly gramophone, if you'll agree that I get the silver tea set.

turns.speaker: Joanne
turns.line: How typical, when are you ever going to use a silver tea set? Fine! I don't want to drag this out any longer than necessary. What's next? What about these old photographs?

turns.speaker: Je
turns.line: Which ones? Let me have a look. Wow, look at that! That brings back memories. . . . That?

turns.speaker: Joanne
turns.line: Our trip to Italy! I remember that day. We were going to visit the Trevi fountain, and we got caught in the rain. . . .

turns.speaker: Je
turns.line: . . . and you looked so adorable with your hair all wet. I had to take a picture of you standing there in that little alley, smiling and laughing in the rain. . . .

turns.speaker: Joanne
turns.line: Oh, we really did have fun back then didn't we?

turns.speaker: Je
turns.line: Oh, Joanne, are we making a big mistake? I know our relationship has been on the rocks for sometime but are you sure we can't reconcile and try again? I still love you.

turns.speaker: Joanne
turns.line: Oh Jeff! I love you too! I'm so glad we didn't have to decide who keeps the motorcycle.

turns.speaker: Je
turns.line: The motorcycle? But that's mine!

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: Thank you for organizing this great baby shower for me! I've always been to baby showers but never actually had one held for me! Let's get started!

turns.speaker: B
turns.line: Ok, let's start opening some presents!

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: Oh look! What a great little bib for the baby! This will definitely come in handy! Oh wow, you also got me a stroller! That's so great! Thank you!

turns.speaker: B
turns.line: This next one is from Betty.

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: A highchair and car seat! Wow Betty thank you so much! I really appreciate it!

turns.speaker: B
turns.line: One more from Carla.

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: A playpen and crib! Thanks Carla! This is just what I needed!

turns.speaker: B
turns.line: OK, that's all of them. No more gifts. Now who wants to guess when the baby is due!

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: Umm. I think my water just broke! Get me to a hospital!

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: How about this floor lamp?

turns.speaker: B
turns.line: Fine just get it! We have been shopping for furniture for five hours! I'm so tired!

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: We still need to find an armoire and a dresser.

turns.speaker: B
turns.line: Fine! I am going to go home and drop off this nightstand, coffee table and love seat while you look for the rest of the things.

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: Great! Pick me up in about an hour because I think I'll also get a bean bag and a dining set.

turns.speaker: B
turns.line: While you are at it can you pick out a nice recliner? I really want one so I can watch TV.

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: Recliner? In my beautifully decorated living room? I don't think so!

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: Car trouble center. How may I help you?

turns.speaker: B
turns.line: My car won't start! Stupid old car!

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: Hold on, before you kick your car let's go through some possible problems.

turns.speaker: B
turns.line: Fine.

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: Ok, first of all, can you turn the key in the ignition?

turns.speaker: B
turns.line: Yeah! I am here with my friend and he thinks it may be the spark plug or the starter motor.

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: Those are possible problems, but tell me, when you turn the key, do you hear the starter motor crank?

turns.speaker: B
turns.line: Yeah, it sounds like it usually does when I start the car, but nothing else happens. The engine won't start. Should I maybe press the accelerator?

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: No. If you step on the accelerator pedal you can flood the carburetor and your car will never start.

turns.speaker: B
turns.line: So what do you think it is?

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: I know this may seem like a silly question, but does your car have gasoline?

turns.speaker: B
turns.line: Umm. yeah! Right! I got the car started! Thanks for your help! I told you to fill the tank!

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: So what's your guys' take on all this global warming hysteria in the media?

turns.speaker: B
turns.line: It's pretty serious, man. There have been tons of scientific studies and the scientific community says that the earth is heating up. We need to make some drastic changes to our lifestyle if we want to preserve our planet.

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: I don't know. It sounds like a bunch of mumbo jumbo if you ask me. "Save the earth!" The earth will save itself. It's survived worst disasters in the past. I mean, honestly, we live in the boonies. There's no way anyone here is ever going to walk or bike to work, especially in the winter. And we have no bus system. My house is forty years old and it would take a lot of money to get it refitted to be "green" and "energy-efficient".

turns.speaker: C
turns.line: Well I don't really know if I believe in global warming either, or whether or not it was our doing or a natural change the earth is going through, but you have to admit that we're living pretty irresponsibly here in the west.

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: I guess...

turns.speaker: C
turns.line: I think the issue at hand is sustainability. We've only got this one earth we can live on, and our resources are quickly disappearing because of our own carelessness and our inability to think of anyone but ourselves and anything but the present.

turns.speaker: B
turns.line: So, like I was saying, we need to change the way we live. We need to reduce our carbon footprint.

turns.speaker: C
turns.line: But it doesn't have to be that drastic. Hybrid vehicles and solar panels are too expensive to be feasible right now. And we don't have to be hippies living off the land and buying everything organic either, though it helps.

turns.speaker: B
turns.line: I car pool to work everyday with some buddies of mine. I have a rain barrel outside my house I use to water my plants and my lawn in the summer, and I make sure I always bring reusable bags with me when I get my groceries. And we just started using bio-degradable plastic made from corn oil for take-out orders at my family's restaurant. Remember the three R's? Reduce. Reuse. Recycle.

turns.speaker: C
turns.line: Exactly, it's just small simple changes, like buying energy-saving light bulbs, starting a compost bin, recycling bottles and papers, using reusable water bottles, stop using disposable cups and cutlery.

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: Like the ones we're drinking out of?

turns.speaker: B
turns.line: Yeah.

turns.speaker: Officer
turns.line: Ok Sally, we have an artist here to help us.

turns.speaker: Brown
turns.line: We'll ask you questions about the bank robber you saw and Paul will draw a picture. Are you ready?

turns.speaker: Sally
turns.line: Yes, hmmm. Well, he had brown hair. . .long hair. . . and he had some facial hair. . . was brown, too.

turns.speaker: Officer
turns.line: Good! Ok, the facial hair, was it a beard or a

turns.speaker: Brown
turns.line: mustache?

turns.speaker: Sally
turns.line: Both! His mustache was very short and thin, . . . . on the top of his lip.

turns.speaker: Paul
turns.line: un-uh hmmm.. . , like this?

turns.speaker: Sally
turns.line: Yes, that's the mustache! But the beard isn't right, mean, it didn't cover his whole face. . . . think it was just on his chin.

turns.speaker: Officer
turns.line: A goatee? Was it like Paul's?

turns.speaker: Sally
turns.line: Ah yes, that's it, he had a goatee.........

turns.speaker: Paul
turns.line: Ok, what about sideburns? Did he have sideburns?

turns.speaker: Sally
turns.line: Um, they were long and thick, yours!

turns.speaker: Paul
turns.line: Alright, was this the man you saw?

turns.speaker: Sally
turns.line: Yes, that's him! Hmmmmm, he looks a lot like you.

turns.speaker: Officer
turns.line: Hmmm, why yes he does. Paul, where were

turns.speaker: Brown
turns.line: you on Friday afternoon?

turns.speaker: Paul
turns.line: What? That's ridiculous! It wasn't me! I didn't do anything.

turns.speaker: MeGee
turns.line: Alright, Officer McGraw, Give it to me straight, what are we looking at here?

turns.speaker: McGraw
turns.line: Detective MeGee! We're glad to see you! We could sure use your expertise on this one. It's a break-in, but nothing seems to have been stolen. We received a call from the Bear family at around ten thirty this morning. They had gone out for a walk before breakfast and came home to this mess! Broken chairs and porridge all over the place! Apparently, Momma Bear had made the porridge a little too hot, you see, and they were waiting for it to cool down. Detective

turns.speaker: MeGee
turns.line: Okay then, let's start examining the evidence. . . . Have the forensics team been in yet?

turns.speaker: McGraw
turns.line: Yes sir. They found some fingerprints on the bowls and are analyzing them back at the lab as we speak. Hopefully, they will be able to identify the burglar soon. Detective

turns.speaker: MeGee
turns.line: Hmmmm,Ah ha! What's this? A strand of golden hair. . . . . . this is a very important piece of trace evidence McGraw. It tells me the suspect has long golden hair. . . . . . . very few men have long golden hair. . . . . . . our criminal could be a woman. . . . . .

turns.speaker: McGraw
turns.line: A woman? Was she working alone? Did she have an accomplice? Detective

turns.speaker: MeGee
turns.line: An accomplice? No, no McGraw, she was definitely working alone. See here, there are footprints in the porridge, here on the floor. . . . footprints, tells me that our suspect is small. . . . could possibly be a child.

turns.speaker: McGraw
turns.line: A child? Surely not, sir. . . Detective

turns.speaker: MeGee
turns.line: We must follow the clues, McGraw! The evidence doesn't lie! Now, let's reconstruct the crime. . . . . . the suspect came in, sat in each chair breaking the smallest one into little pieces. Next, the porridge. she obviously tried to eat it and because it was so hot, she dropped it on the floor. . . . this mess. interesting. These footprints seem to lead upstairs. McGraw, did your officers clear the scene?

turns.speaker: McGraw
turns.line: Well, there was no one down here. . . andmaybe we forget to check upstairs. Goldylocks: Hey! What's with all the noise? I'm trying tosleep up here! Detective

turns.speaker: MeGee
turns.line: There she is! Get her!

turns.speaker: Sammy
turns.line: Alright, let's run through this one more time from the top. I will be positioned here, across from the bank on this park bench. Now, according to the intel we got from Jimmy. . .

turns.speaker: Ralph
turns.line: ah, who's Jimmy?

turns.speaker: Sammy
turns.line: Jeez Ralph! Pay attention, will ya? Jimmy's our mole, you know. . . . the guy on the inside. . . He's been snooping and passing on the info to us so we can pull this heist off!

turns.speaker: Frankie
turns.line: Yea, Ralph, clean the moth balls outta your ears and listen up. This here is important , you don't wanna end up back in the slammer, do ya? Your role is pretty important here, we're depending on you, man.

turns.speaker: Ralph
turns.line: Ok, ok! I'm listening! moth balls, hrumph. . .

turns.speaker: Sammy
turns.line: Alright then, . . . . was I? Oh yeah, ok, so I'll be the lookout. . . . here on the bench across from the bank. Nobody moves until I give the go-ahead, Alright? And what's the goahead? . . . Ralph?

turns.speaker: Ralph
turns.line: You, umm. . . ah. . . . yeah, you'll take off your hat and scratch your head!

turns.speaker: Sammy
turns.line: Right. When I take my hat off and scratch my head, you do what?

turns.speaker: Ralph
turns.line: I get in the box.

turns.speaker: Frankie
turns.line: Right, you get in the box. I'll make sure it's all sealed and then, posing as a delivery guy, I'll drop off a ‘special package' for the manager. Now, according to Jimmy, the bank manager is leaving early on Tuesday 'cause it's his wedding anniversary. He and the wife are having a romantic rendezvous in the country, so any packages delivered will be left unopened in his office until he gets back late on Wednesday. . . .

turns.speaker: Sammy
turns.line: . . . . . . Which gives us access to his office for at least Come hours. . . . Ralph, this is where you come in. . . . where are you?

turns.speaker: Ralph
turns.line: I'm standing right next to you Sammy, Sorry Sam, I'm in the box. Right there. . . in that box.

turns.speaker: Frankie
turns.line: . . . . what do you do once I deliver you to the manager's office?

turns.speaker: Ralph
turns.line: I stay in the box until the bank has closed, . I get out of the box.

turns.speaker: Sammy
turns.line: . . . . then? What next, Ralph? Oh for Pete's sake! This is never going to work.

turns.speaker: Ralph
turns.line: Hey, give me a chance here, fellas! I, um, I crack the safe . then, thenI take the money. . . . then I. . . ummmmm, I get back in the box.

turns.speaker: Frankie
turns.line: 'Atta boy Ralph! In the morning I come back to the bank, say there's been a mix-up with the delivery I made and take the ‘special package' back here.

turns.speaker: Sammy
turns.line: Alright, let's get some sleep. . . it's a big day tomorrow fellas!

turns.speaker: Frankie
turns.line: A perfect plan, Sammy! It went off without a hitch!

turns.speaker: Sammy
turns.line: Let's open this up and get Ralph out here so we can start counting the money!

turns.speaker: Ralph
turns.line: Phew! I sure am glad to see you guys! I was sure getting lonely with no one to talk.

turns.speaker: Frankie
turns.line: That's nice, ok how much!

turns.speaker: Ralph
turns.line: Huh?Uh,, really, really, really glad?

turns.speaker: Sammy
turns.line: Money, Ralph! Money!

turns.speaker: Ralph
turns.line: Oh man, I knew I forgot something. . . . . . .

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: Ok Mark, it's your turn to ring the doorbell. I did it last time.

turns.speaker: B
turns.line: I hate going door to door, and I hate asking for money.

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: But we need to raise enough money for the school fundraiser so that our class can win the pizza party! You do want to have a pizza party, don't you?

turns.speaker: B
turns.line: Yes, but...

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: Just go already!

turns.speaker: B
turns.line: No one's coming.

turns.line: Try again.

turns.speaker: B
turns.line: Maybe there's no one home.

turns.line: Of course there's someone home! There are two cars in the driveway and I see lights on in the house! Hello! Anybody home? We would like to know if you want to sponsor us in our school fundraiser. Fifty percent of the profits go towards the new school playground!

turns.speaker: B
turns.line: I don't know why anyone would want what's in this catalog anyway. It's just a bunch of tacky Christmas ornaments, Cd's of old people singing Christmas songs, and special crackers and cheeses and boxes of chocolates.

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: You don't like chocolates?

turns.speaker: B
turns.line: Not this kind. They've got weird names like ganache and praline.

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: Look! I just saw someone walking around inside! These people are being very rude!

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: Finally, someone's coming!

turns.speaker: B
turns.line: They don't look too happy.

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: Hi, sir. Would you like to sponsor us or make a donation to.

turns.speaker: C
turns.line: What grade are you kids in?

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: Grade seven.

turns.speaker: C
turns.line: Then for goodness sake, don't you see this sign? Can't you read?

turns.line: No soliciting.

turns.line: What does that mean?

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: No idea.

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: Trina, will you marry me?

turns.speaker: B
turns.line: Yes! Yes! And yes! Jared of course I'll marry you!

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: Oh Babe, I can't wait to spend the rest of my life with you! I can't wait for all the adventures we're going to have, for all the fights and the laughter. I can't wait to grow old and wrinkly with you.

turns.speaker: B
turns.line: Oh Jared! I can't wait for our wedding! I hope you don't mind, but I've already chosen a date! Six months from now in the summer! Melissa saw you buying the ring last month so I've had plenty of time to start planning!

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: She what?

turns.speaker: B
turns.line: Oh don't worry sweetie, I didn't know when you were going to propose. It was still a nice surprise! As I was saying, I've got it all planned out. There's almost nothing left to do! I wrote up our guest list and we will have roughly four hundred guests attending.

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: four hundred?

turns.speaker: B
turns.line: No need to sweat it. My parents agreed to pay for most of the wedding, which is going to be low budget anyway. So roughly four hundred people, which means that the hall at Northwood Heights will be our reception venue. I thought it would be nice if we had the wedding at your parents' church and my uncle of course would be officiating. We'll meet with him soon for some pre-wedding counseling. The music for the wedding ceremony was a no-brainer. My step-sister and her string quartet will take care of that. My cousin will be the official photographer. I thought it would also be nice if his daughter could sing a solo. Did you know that she's going to be a professional opera singer?

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: Ah...

turns.speaker: B
turns.line: And then of course the ladies at the church would love to be our caterers for the banquet and we'll get the Youth Group to serve us. I was thinking that your friend's band could be our entertainment for the night. though they might have to tone it down a bit. Or we could hire a DJ. Your sister's husband could get us a discount with that company that does the decor at weddings. What's their name again? I was thinking that we could have an island paradise- themed wedding and our theme color would be a soothing blue like Aquamarine. And there will be a huge seashell on the wall behind the podium where we'll make our toasts! What do you think of small packages of drink mixes for our wedding favors? Who else am I missing? Oh, your uncle could be our florist and his wife could make our wedding cake!

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: Wow.

turns.speaker: B
turns.line: See? It's going to be wonderful! Oh this wedding is going to be everything I ever dreamed of.

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: If I survive the next six months.

turns.line: Oh, George, what a beautiful day it is today! The sun is hot and there are just a few clouds scattered here and there! What a perfect day to be at the beach! The kids are going to have so much fun! And we'll be able to relax in the sun while they're playing.

turns.speaker: B
turns.line: It does seem like the perfect day! I'm glad we chose to get out of the city and enjoy the nice weather! This looks like the perfect spot! Ok kids, put on your sunscreen while your mom and I set up camp. Here, Mary, help me lay down these beach towels.

turns.line: There we go. Can you help me with the umbrella? Perfect.

turns.speaker: B
turns.line: Ok kids, here's a beach ball and a Frisbee, a pail and a shovel. I want to see an impressive sandcastle by the time we leave. Don't stray too far. Wait! Leave your sandals here or put on your wet shoes.

turns.line: And stay in the shallow area. I don't want to see you go any farther than that sandbar! It's too deep out there and we didn't bring your floaties.

turns.speaker: B
turns.line: You're back already? The water was too cold, huh? I'll tell you a secret. Do you see that small pool of water over there? It'll be warmer in there. Go see if you can find some seashells or catch some minnows.

turns.line: What is that? A jellyfish? Jeremy, put that down right now! It could sting you!

turns.line: Well, then how about these? What is this style called?

turns.line: I don't know. Would they go with your clothes? The backs are really high. and the way the tongue just sticks up. They're almost like a boot. And the sole doesn't look like it would have a very good grip.

turns.line: They're only forty-five dollars! And they've got cool fluorescent orange shoelaces! Mom?

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: Cheese is usually categorized intofour types: soft, semi- soft semi-hard and hard. The designation refers to the amount of moisture in the cheese, which directly affects its texture. Making cheese is an ancient practice, dating back thousands of years, and the home cheese maker can usually find recipes for cheese that falls into any of the four categories.

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: Soft cheese includes cottage cheese, cream cheese, ricotta, brie, bleu, roquefort, mozzarella, meunster and similar cheeses. These cheeses generally pair well with fruit or meats, or can be used as breakfast cheeses in an omelette Nor as pasta fillings. They are usually mildly flavored and very high in moisture.

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: American, Colby, co-jack and similar cheeses are inthe semi-soft category. These are slightly stronger in flavor and cover a wide range of uses. Co-jack cheese, a blend of Colby and Monterrey jack is one of the most popular. This allows the sharper flavor of Colby to be combined with the milder jack cheese, and also melts better than plain Colby. Grilled cheese sandwiches often use American cheese, and Mexican cheeses such as Asadero and Queso Fresco are becoming more popular.

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: Hard cheeses include Parmesan, Romano, Asiago, Swiss, Gruyere and others. Parmesan and Romano are most familiar as the grated powder used to top spaghetti, but they are also used as accompaniments for fruit, wine, nuts and other appetizer items. Swiss is a popular sandwich cheese and melts well, unlike some other hard cheeses.

turns.line: Then here we have a series of deductions. First off are the federal ones. FICA stands for Federal Insurance Contribution Act, or something like that. It's your federal income tax. And then there's Social Security and Medicare, which are both federal programs to help you out after you retire or if you were unable to work.

turns.line: All right, I see. So the Medicare isn't actually a health insurance I can use now.

title: The Night Before Christmas
narration: It was the night before Christmas, when all through the house Not a creature was stirring, not even a mouse; The stockings were hung bythe chimney with care, In hopes that St. Nicholas soon would be there; The children were nestled all snug in their beds, And mama in her 'kerchief, and I in my cap, Had just settled down for a long winter's nap, When out on the lawn there arose such a clatter, I sprang from the bed to see what was the matter. Away to the window I flew like a flash, Tore open the shutters and threw up the sash. The moon on the breast of the new-fallen snow Gave the lustre of mid-day to objects below, When, what to my wondering eyes should appear, But a miniature sleigh, and eight tiny reindeer, With a little old driver, so lively and quick, I knew in a moment it must be St. Nick. More rapid than eagles his coursers they came, And he whistled, and shouted, and called them by name; " Now, Dasher! now, Dancer! now, Prancer and Vixen! On, Comet! on Cupid! on, Donder and Blitzen! To the top of the porch! to the top of the wall! Now dash away! dash away! dash away all! As dry leaves that before the wild hurricane fly, When they meet with an obstacle, mount to the sky, So up to the house-top the coursers they flew, With the sleigh full of toys, and St. Nicholas too. And then, in a twinkling, I heard on the roof. The prancing and pawing of each little hoof. As I drew in my head, and was turning around, Down the chimney St. Nicholas came with a bound. He was dressed all in fur, from his head to his foot, And his clothes were all tarnished with ashes and soot; A bundle of toys he had flung on his back, And he looked like a peddler just opening his pack. His eyes – how they twinkled! his dimples how merry! His cheeks were like roses, his nose like a cherry! His droll little mouth was drawn up like a bow, Andthe beard of his chin was as white as the snow; The stump of a pipe he held tight in his teeth, Andthe smoke it encircled his head like a wreath; He had a broad face and a little round belly, That shook, when he laughed like a bowlful of jelly. He was chubby and plump, a right jolly old elf, And I laughed when I saw him, in spite of myself; A wink of his eye and a twist of his head, Soon gave me to know I had nothing to dread; He spoke not a word, but went straight to his work, And filled allthe thestockings; then turned with a jerk, And laying his finger aside of his nose, And giving a nod, upthe chimney he rose; He sprang to his sleigh, to his team gave a whistle, And away they all flew like the down of a thistle. But I heard him exclaim, ere he drove out of sight, " Christmas to all, and to all a good-night.

turns.line: No!

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: Come on! I'll pay you back on Tuesday.

turns.speaker: B
turns.line: Last time I lent you money, you never paid me back.

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: I promise if you lend me five dollars today, I will repay you in full next week.

turns.speaker: B
turns.line: Ok, but I'm taking your skateboard as collateral.

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: Fine! I can't believe you don't trust me.

turns.speaker: B
turns.line: It's nothing personal, just business.

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: Help me organize these coins.

turns.speaker: B
turns.line: That's a lot of money! What did you do? Break the piggy bank?

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: Yeah, I'm gonna go to the bank and change it for bills, but first I have to separate them into little piles.

turns.speaker: B
turns.line: Ok, I'll find all the quarters and dimes while you sort the nickels and pennies.

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: Great, then we can add everything up and take it to the bank.

turns.speaker: B
turns.line: I found some coins that are not from here.

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: Oh yeah, those are from my trip to London. I have a couple of different pence, but in all it won't add up to one pound.

turns.speaker: B
turns.line: Are you sure the bank will change these coins for you?

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: Hopefully!

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: Bruno Bistro, how may I help you?

turns.speaker: B
turns.line: Yes hello, I would like to make a reservation please.

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: Certainly sir, For which day and time please?

turns.speaker: B
turns.line: Tonight at seven.

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: I'm sorry sir, but we are fully booked tonight until eight.

turns.speaker: B
turns.line: In that case, eight o'clock is fine.

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: Very well, and how many people will attend tonight?

turns.speaker: B
turns.line: Four people.

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: Lastly, may I please know what name I should make the reservation under?

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: Mark.

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: Why didn't you text me last night?

turns.speaker: B
turns.line: What? I sent you three or four messages!

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: I didn't get any of them. I was waiting for you to text me the address of where the party was and I never got your message.

turns.speaker: B
turns.line: Why didn't you just call? I hate sending SMS messages.

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: Well, because I didn't have any credit on my phone. I used it all up this month.

turns.speaker: B
turns.line: I thought you had an unlimited SMS plan?

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: I do, but if I don't have any credit in my phone, it won't let me call or send messages.

turns.speaker: B
turns.line: No wonder you didn't get my texts!

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: I got an urgent email from Tom! He says he is in London and got robbed and needs us to wire him some money for his hotel.

turns.speaker: B
turns.line: What? That sounds really dodgy tome.

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: No way, Tom is an honest person, he wouldn't lie tome.

turns.speaker: B
turns.line: No I mean, it seems like someone may have hacked his email account and sent that out. I mean think about it, why would he email you instead of calling you.

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: Do you really think someone is trying to scam people into sending money?

turns.speaker: B
turns.line: For sure! There are so many con artists out there, you never really know.

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: Have you read all these crazy things that are going on around the world?

turns.speaker: B
turns.line: What do you mean?

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: I was reading about how some people get tricked or drugged in their hotel rooms and have their organs removed! Then they are sold on the black market.

turns.speaker: B
turns.line: Don't tell me you actually believe all that? Don't be so gullible, they are just urban legends. They are just stories people make up to scare you.

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: Well, I was also reading about how some popular songs have subliminal or even satanic messages if you play them backwards! Can you believe that?

turns.speaker: B
turns.line: You really think an artist or songwriter is going to go through the trouble of putting subliminal or satanic messages in a song? Don't be so naive!

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: Well maybe you are right, but how about the story of how KFC has rows of headless chickens which are super grown in order to get bigger chickens faster!

turns.speaker: B
turns.line: Sounds a bit too far fetched to be true don't you think?

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: I'm hungry, let's order up something to eat.

turns.speaker: B
turns.line: Ok, maybe we can order a soup and a salad from the restaurant down the street.

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: I was thinking of getting a hamburger, fries and a chocolate sundae.

turns.speaker: B
turns.line: You eat too much junk food. That sort of stuff clogs up your arteries and is very high in cholesterol.

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: Well I never seem to gain weight so I don't mind.

turns.speaker: B
turns.line: It's not only about getting fat or not, it's about being healthy. You could really have some health problems later on.

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: How about pizza or maybe some fried chicken! Better yet, let's order some hot dogs!

turns.speaker: B
turns.line: You are a lost cause.

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: Are you ok? You seem a bit anxious.

turns.speaker: B
turns.line: Yeah I'm OK, I have been having a lot of mood swings lately. I think it has to do with the pills my doctor prescribed that are causing chaos on my hormones.

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: So you mean you feel ecstatic one minute and then blue the next?

turns.speaker: B
turns.line: Yeah, it's weird. For example just this morning I was feeling detached and lonely, even though there was really no reason to feel that way.

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: Well, maybe your mood will swing positively and you will feel confident, brave and hopeful!

turns.speaker: B
turns.line: I hope you are right.

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: Why did your girlfriend break up with you?

turns.speaker: B
turns.line: I don't know, she said she was tired of me not manning up and being more independent, which I think is all a bunch of crap.

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: Well, you still live with your parents, so she does have a point.

turns.speaker: B
turns.line: What do you mean? Lots of people live with their parents, especially when rent is so expensive and the slump in the economy.

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: Yeah, but you are almost forty! Plus, you make good money so there is really no excuse. It's simply because you are a momma's boy.

turns.speaker: B
turns.line: Whatever dude, I have everything I need, why would I move out! Have a great roof over my head, my mom does my laundry and cooks for me, what else could a guy ask for!

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: Let's agree to disagree.

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: Can you help me write a newspaper ad?

turns.speaker: B
turns.line: Sure, what are you looking to buy or sell?

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: Actually, I want to hire someone to help me around the house.

turns.speaker: B
turns.line: Oh, you want to get a maid?

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: Well, I think it's better if you call her a cleaning lady or domestic help.

turns.speaker: B
turns.line: Ok, so what do you want her to do?

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: Well, let's see. I want her to come in three times a week for a couple of hours to clean the kitchen, bathroom and maybe do some cooking.

turns.speaker: B
turns.line: Got it. And how much do you offer per month?

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: I would pay her hourly, I don't know what the going rate is though.

turns.speaker: B
turns.line: I know for sure it's more than minimum wage but maybe you should just negotiate with the person that answers the ad.

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: Great! Thanks for your help!

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: Kevin, what is this mess? It looks like a pigsty in here! Clean this up!

turns.speaker: B
turns.line: Ok dad, I will do it in a minute, let me just finish this level of this game.

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: No, I said now! Plus, you are grounded, you're not allowed to play video games. I want you to make your bed, do the laundry and then come downstairs and sweep the floors.

turns.speaker: B
turns.line: That's so unfair!

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: You have to pull your weight around here young man. My house, my rules.

turns.speaker: B
turns.line: But I already mopped the floors, dusted the furniture and vacuumed the rugs!

turns.speaker: A
turns.line: That's great, but you still have work to do, so get to it.
